people.cause: burned out his foundation holding a rite for the hermitage in the dry winter of 1186 (age 68)
people.role: Keeper of the abbey's grain rolls under the prior; walked out to the grove in 1180 and died there
people.backstory: Wrote the grain rolls for Thời Tri Tiết (thoi_tri_tiet) for forty years; devout, he walked out to the grove with Hà Tĩnh Cần (ha_tinh_can) in 1180, and in the dry winter of 1186 he held a rite for the hermitage past what his foundation could bear and was its first grave.

ties.note: the prior whose rolls he kept

people.role: The abbess's attendant at the rite ground
people.appearance: Two rite-pole calluses across each palm; she counts her breaths aloud in a whisper.
people.backstory: Holds the rite poles for Dương Hảo Vũ (duong_hao_vu) at every great rite and has counted its cost in her mistress's breath; she gives her the prior's pills each morning, and hands the one in three the abbess keeps back to the rice cart for the grove.

ties.note: held the poles beside her for sixty years; the kept-back pills go to her

people.role: A Tower reject who walked to the abbey
people.appearance: Bell-shaped birthmark on his neck, rubbed raw whenever a bell is mentioned.
people.backstory: The Tower's Bell Test rang for him and then stopped; he walked down to the abbey, as Thiều Mộ Canh (thieu_mo_canh) did, was sent on to the grove to learn the poles, and is still angry at a bell. A gate-stall orphan, he splits a barrel lid with his fist whenever a bell is mocked, and the grove calls it temper.

people.role: Rain-caller at the abbey's house in Thu Trì
people.appearance: Her left middle finger is dyed blue from the Thu Trì stalls; she tucks it away when buyers look.
people.backstory: Has more Water than Wood and so calls rain in the old way, from the river, at the rain-callers' house under Lã Tiềm Dạ (la_tiem_da); the Night Rain Market's buyers ask for her by name. On the night Lã was to call for the dyers she let the river rain fail, so that her own call the next night would be the one they wanted; Lã took the curses.

people.appearance: Stammers on hard consonants, with soil packed for good under his nails; he laughs at a joke a half-beat after the room has moved on.
people.backstory: Weeds the herb beds for Lam Nhuận Chi (lam_nhuan_chi); one herb in the abbess's pills he cannot name, and the prior's man brings it in sealed jars. Slow to learn any herb, he counts the jars aloud every night and swears to the prior that a thief is at the beds, never working out that it is himself; Tần Xuân Duẩn (tan_xuan_duan) was docked two days' rice for it.

people.appearance: Chipped front tooth; her voice rasps at the top of every note.
people.backstory: Sings the planting song loudest in Ương Ca, which is how the abbey found her at her first planting in 1197; her village sings to drown the graves of Thu Phần, and she wants to know what the graves sing back.

ties.note: the Ương Ca singer the graves took

people.role: Pole-cutter in the lightning-bamboo grove, of the hermitage
people.appearance: Bare feet scarred from split cane; a streak of lightning-white hair at the left temple.
people.backstory: Born in the grove the year the hermitage came (1180), he cuts the struck bamboo with Sở Lôi Duẩn (so_loi_duan) and carries the poles to Hà Tĩnh Cần's (ha_tinh_can) rite ground; he has seen his master walk into the grove before a storm and come out after it.

ties.note: the hermitage's rite master; he carries her poles
